messages.subject: Genetic_Map
parts:
Hi Karl, 

I would like to generate genetic maps of RIL population, which is F7 generation. I have 1 Mb bin map position as markers. I have nearly 750 progenies. As I searched in google group and manual, I did not see straightforward codes/methods to load and run these data using QTL2. I need genetic maps to validate reference assembles. I do not have any phenotype now, I. I need suggestion, how can I format this input file. What I need to do if I don't have phenotype. Do I need to give chromosome information or we can simply get linkage groups using de novo mapping.  I have attached the genotyping file here, the first column is marker and 4th row is accessions. Any suggestions appreciated!


Best
Laxman

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Genetic_Map
parts:
If you're interested in R/qtl2, you should post to https://groups.google.com/group/Rqtl2-disc
There are example R/qtl2 data files for the mouse BXD RIL, which would be similar: https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/main/BXD
And you can just skip the phenotype data.

But for biparental RIL, R/qtl1 should be sufficient.
You'd format the file similar to the files https://rqtl.org/sampledata/
You can just use line ID as the one phenotype.

For either, you need to provide chromosome IDs and positions. And if you have a physical map, I see no value in trying de novo mapping.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Genetic_Map
parts:
R/qtl1 wants positions in cM. If you don't have cM positions, provide your best approximation. For example, just give Mbp positions, or use some approximation of the overall cM:Mbp recombination rate to convert to estimated cM.

Once you've read the cross into R with read.cross(), use est.map() to get estimated inter-marker positions in cM, and then replace.map() to plug them back into the cross object.

karl
